description:
We are VitalSync! 🚀 

We are a passionate team of students from Al Iman School, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026!

Our mission is to develop innovative software to monitor astronauts' health during space missions.

We are interested in space, programming, AI, and creative problem-solving. We welcome members with coding, UI/UX, and data analysis skills.

We're excited to learn, collaborate, have fun, and aim for success! 

VitalSync — Every Beat Matters, Even in Space.
summary:
AVITA is an intelligent astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support system for long-duration space missions. Radiation, altered gravity, isolation, confinement, and closed environments can affect astronauts' physical health, mental well-being, sleep, and performance.

AVITA brings four connected capabilities into one platform: **Monitor, Explore, Adapt, and Understand.**

**Monitor** tracks 18 health indicators through wearable readings and daily check-ins, including heart rate, sleep, activity, mood, stress, and fatigue, helping astronauts notice changes from personal baselines. **Explore** includes an interactive body viewer linked to NASA's space hazards and Mission Twin, where astronauts test what-if changes to sleep, exercise, hydration, and recovery. **Adapt** supports daily routine planning with suggestions that respect mission constraints. **Understand** explains health trends, alerts, and guidance using NASA research.

For our prototype, we used **Python and Google Colab** to process Earth-based LifeSnaps health data and four historical NASA data files covering environmental conditions, radiation, and statistics. **React and AI Studio** helped us transform the data into interactive visualizations and guidance.

AVITA aims to strengthen health awareness, encourage earlier recognition of changes, and support informed decisions, helping astronauts become more independent far from Earth.
